security_audit.summary: Static analysis produced many alerts, but review found they are documentation examples, placeholder URLs, normal presentation file output, or markdown formatting artifacts. No prompt injection, credential handling, hidden exfiltration, or malicious automation intent was found in the cited files.

remediation.issue: Example API fetches do not show request timeouts or source validation.
remediation.suggestion: Add a timeout and advise users to allow only trusted API URLs before generating slides from remote data.

remediation.issue: Bulk generation examples derive output filenames from data rows.
remediation.suggestion: Sanitize filenames and prevent path separators before saving per-record presentations.

remediation.issue: Installation examples include shell commands inside markdown.
remediation.suggestion: Keep install commands explicit and document that users should review commands before running them.

content.value_statement: Building polished PowerPoint decks by hand is slow and hard to repeat. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through PPTX creation, editing, and automation with python-pptx.
actual_capabilities: Creates new .pptx files with title, content, bullet, and conclusion slides.
Edits existing presentations by updating text, placeholders, slide order, and output files.
Adds charts, tables, images, hyperlinks, formatted text, and custom shapes.
Applies templates, themes, brand colors, slide sizes, and layout guidance.
Generates decks in bulk from CSV, JSON, SQLite databases, or API data.
Provides helper functions for title, bullet, image, chart, table, and branded slides.
limitations: Requires Python and the python-pptx library in the working environment.
Some advanced PowerPoint features depend on python-pptx support and may need manual review.
Does not automatically verify external API sources, database contents, or input data quality.
Generated decks should be opened in PowerPoint to confirm layout, fonts, and compatibility.

use_cases.title: Automate Business Reports
use_cases.description: Generate weekly or monthly decks from spreadsheets, charts, and summary tables.

use_cases.title: Create Branded Sales Decks
use_cases.description: Build consistent client presentations from a template with approved colors and layouts.

use_cases.title: Prepare Teaching Materials
use_cases.description: Turn structured lesson content into slides with images, tables, and clear visual hierarchy.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Deck
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a small presentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PowerPoint deck about [topic] with a title slide, three content slides, and a closing slide. Use concise bullets.

prompt_templates.title: Add Data Visuals
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a .pptx report from this data: [paste data]. Include one bar chart, one table, and a short insight slide.

prompt_templates.title: Edit an Existing Presentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [file name] and update the deck for [audience]. Replace outdated text, improve slide order, and save a revised copy.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Branded Deck from Data
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using template and bulk generation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [template file] and [data file] to generate a branded presentation. Apply our colors, create charts, and produce one slide per record.

output_examples.input: A sales manager asks for a quarterly revenue review from a CSV file.
output_examples.output: A PowerPoint deck with a title slide, revenue trend chart, regional table, key findings slide, and next steps.

output_examples.input: A consultant asks to rebrand an existing client presentation.
output_examples.output: An updated .pptx file with revised colors, consistent fonts, corrected placeholders, and a new summary slide.

output_examples.input: An educator asks for a lesson deck about renewable energy.
output_examples.output: A structured classroom presentation with topic slides, image placeholders, comparison tables, and a review slide.

best_practices: Start from a template when brand consistency matters.
Validate data before creating charts or bulk-generated slides.
Open the generated .pptx file to check layout, fonts, and image placement.
anti_patterns: Do not pack slides with long paragraphs or too many visual elements.
Do not use untrusted API data or database queries without review.
Do not overwrite the original presentation without saving a separate copy.

faq.question: Can this skill create a PowerPoint file from scratch?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide creation of new .pptx files with slides, text, images, tables, and charts.

faq.question: Can it edit an existing deck?
faq.answer: Yes. It can update text, reorder slides, use templates, and save a revised presentation.

faq.question: Does it require Microsoft PowerPoint?
faq.answer: No for generation. It uses python-pptx, but PowerPoint is useful for final visual review.

faq.question: Can it create charts from spreadsheet data?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for charts, tables, and reports based on CSV or other structured data.

faq.question: Can it use company templates?
faq.answer: Yes. It can load a template .pptx and create slides using the template layouts.

faq.question: Is generated formatting always perfect?
faq.answer: No. Fonts, spacing, and compatibility should be checked in PowerPoint before sharing.
